official_measurement_examples.name: Scheduled Monument Consent separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England's 26 May 2026 guidance states written Scheduled Monument Consent is required before most works to a scheduled monument and planning permission may also be separately required.

official_measurement_examples.name: Current national dataset
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's 24 July 2026 scheduled-monument dataset contains Historic England designation geometry and identifies Historic England as the sole provider.

official_measurement_examples.name: NHLE official register
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England describes the National Heritage List for England as the official up-to-date register of nationally protected historic buildings and sites.

official_measurement_examples.name: GIS refresh timing
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England's open-data page reports Scheduled Monuments GIS last updated 14 July 2026, so older copied geometry must not silently override the current release.

official_measurement_examples.name: Visible remains limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Scheduled monuments can include buried archaeology and are not necessarily ancient or visible above ground, so visual inspection cannot establish absence.

official_measurement_examples.name: Archaeology beyond scheduling
official_measurement_examples.fact: Historic England Advice Note 17 addresses archaeology through the planning system; unscheduled archaeological interest remains distinct from statutory scheduling.

official_measurement_examples.name: Setting distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning assessment of a proposal affecting a monument's setting is distinct from works physically requiring Scheduled Monument Consent within the scheduled area.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permission separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Scheduled Monument Consent, planning permission, archaeological investigation conditions and heritage significance assessment are separate controls and none alone establishes parcel development capacity.

core_rules: scheduled-monument geometry is designation evidence not a complete planning decision
Scheduled Monument Consent is distinct from planning permission
planning permission does not replace Scheduled Monument Consent where it is required
absence of visible remains is not proof no scheduled or unscheduled archaeology exists
NHLE current designation data should take precedence over stale copied geometry
an indicative map display must not replace the official list entry and legal schedule
archaeological potential is distinct from scheduled-monument designation
a monument setting effect can extend beyond the scheduled polygon
local archaeological priority areas are not national scheduling
heritage significance assessment must retain proposal and asset context
Class Consent or other exceptions must not be presumed without matching legal facts
archaeological investigation conditions are not development-capacity evidence
heritage protection does not determine land ownership access rights or utility capacity
historic datasets must retain date source and designation status
no parcel archaeology clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
